title: Personality plus
goals: Describe a person using personality adjectives and their opposites (reliable / unreliable, patient / impatient).
Say how someone does things using adverbs of manner (carefully, quietly, well, fast).
Tell adjectives and adverbs apart, and use adjectives after be, feel, get and sound.
Add emphasis with intensifiers: pretty, extremely, absolutely, not … at all.
Talk about annoying habits with always + present continuous, and point out the good side with at least.
Write a profile of a person you admire.

learn.title: Adjective or adverb of manner
learn.html:
An adjective describes a noun (a careful driver). An adverb of manner describes a verb and says how something is done (drives carefully). In Spanish, adverbs usually end in -mente; in English, they end in -ly.

RuleAdjective → Adverb
Regular: + -lypatient → patiently, careful → carefully, quiet → quietly, serious → seriously
Ends in -y: y → i + -lyeasy → easily, noisy → noisily
Ends in -ic: + -allyautomatic → automatically
Irregulargood → well
Same as the adjectivefast → fast, hard → hard, late → late

Position: the adverb goes after the verb or its object: She drives carefully. He speaks English very fast.

Watch out: hardly and lately exist, but they do NOT mean “hard” or “late”: hardly = almost not; lately = recently.

watch.why: A verb is described with an adverb, not an adjective.
The adverb of good is well.
Hardly means “almost not”; hard is both an adjective and an adverb.

learn.title: be, feel, get, sound + adjective
learn.html:
After verbs of state or perception (be, feel, get, sound, look, seem, smell, taste) you use an adjective, not an adverb. They describe the person or thing, not the action.

IncorrectCorrect
I feel safely with her.I feel safe with her.
He gets recklessly sometimes.He gets reckless sometimes.
His voice sounds terribly.His voice sounds terrible.

Exception: when feel means “to have an opinion”, you use an adverb: I feel strongly about it (I have strong views about it).

watch.wrong: I feel strong about this issue.
watch.right: I feel strongly about this issue.
watch.why: Feel = to have an opinion: adverb strongly.

learn.title: Intensifiers: very, really, absolutely…
learn.html:
They go before an adjective or adverb to change its strength.

FunctionWordsExample
Strongervery, really, extremely, incredibly, soShe's extremely generous. We get along very well.
“More than a little”pretty, fairlyHe's pretty easygoing.
100 %completely, totallyHe's completely honest.
With adjectives that are already strong (wonderful, fantastic, terrible)absolutely, really (NOT very)She's absolutely wonderful.
Strong negative(not) … at all, after the adjectiveShe's not selfish at all.

watch.why: Wonderful is already strong: don't use very.

watch.wrong: He's not at all selfish very.
watch.why: At all goes after the adjective.
Well is a normal adverb: it goes with very, really or incredibly.

learn.title: Prefixes for the opposite: un-, in-, dis-
learn.html:
A prefix goes at the start of a word and turns it into its opposite. Each adjective uses its own prefix, so you have to learn them.

PrefixAdjective → Opposite
un-friendly → unfriendly, reliable → unreliable, happy → unhappy
im- / in-patient → impatient, considerate → inconsiderate
dis-honest → dishonest, organized → disorganized

Before p use im- (impatient), not in-.

watch.wrong: She is not organized, she is unorganized.

learn.title: always + present continuous: annoying habits
learn.html:
With always + present continuous (be + verb-ing) you talk about something someone does very often, usually an annoying habit. It can also be a funny or special habit.

UseExample
Annoying habitMy roommate is always borrowing my things.
Habit in the pastHe was always talking about people behind their backs.
Nice habitShe's always smiling.

Position: always goes after be and before the verb-ing. Compare: He always borrows my pen (a neutral fact) with He's always borrowing my pen (it bothers me).

To point out the good side of something, use at least: He's always late. Well, at least he's honest.

watch.wrong: He's always to borrow my car.
watch.why: After always + be, use a verb with -ing.
At last means “finally”; at least means “at least”.

learn.title: Useful expressions for describing someone
learn.html:
• She's incredibly talented. — praise with an intensifier.
  • He's pretty easygoing. — “quite” easygoing.
  • She's not selfish at all. — strong negative.
  • You can count on him. — you can rely on him.
  • He's always wasting time. Well, at least he's pleasant. — complaint + positive side.
  • I can be pretty shy. — I can be + adjective: “sometimes I am”.
  • We get along very well. — we get on very well.
  • I feel strongly about it. — I have a firm opinion.

write.prompt: Write a text of 120 to 180 words about a person you admire (a relative, friend or boss). Describe their personality with intensifiers (incredibly, really, totally, not … at all), say how they do things with adverbs of manner (carefully, patiently, well), and mention one of their habits with always + present continuous. Opening example: I really admire my aunt Rosa because she's incredibly generous…
checklist: At least 4 personality adjectives, two of them with an intensifier (not … at all after the adjective)
At least 3 adverbs of manner after the verb
One habit with always + be + verb-ing
One opposite with a prefix (impatient, dishonest…)
Use of at least to point out a positive side
write.model:
I really admire my aunt Rosa because she's incredibly generous. She always helps people who need something, and she does it quietly, without asking for anything. She's also totally honest, and she's not selfish at all. When my cousin lost his job, she listened to him patiently and gave him money to pay his rent.

My aunt works carefully and speaks politely to everyone. She cooks really well, too! She feels calm in difficult situations. Of course, nobody is perfect. She's always losing her keys, and she's always calling me late at night to ask where they are! She can be a bit impatient when she is hungry, but at least she is never rude.

She is not boring at all. She gets excited about new ideas, and she dances happily at every party. I hope I can be as kind as she is when I'm older. At least I'm learning from the best teacher I know.

write.prompt: Write a message of 120 to 150 words to a roommate or coworker. Kindly tell them two things about their habits that bother you (always + present continuous) and two good things about them. Use “at least” at least once. Opening example: Hi Paco, I want to talk about a few things…
checklist: Two annoying habits with always + be + verb-ing
Two positive qualities with an intensifier
at least to point out the positive side
One adverb of manner (quietly, carefully, on time)
write.model:
Hi Paco,

I want to talk about a few things, and I hope you won't be upset. You're a great roommate, and I'm really glad we live together. First, you're incredibly kind, and you always help me with my shopping. Also, you're really funny, so the apartment is never boring.

But there are two small problems. You're always leaving your dirty dishes in the sink, and you're always playing music loudly late at night. I get tired in the morning because I can't sleep well. Could you please wash your dishes and use headphones after ten o'clock?

At least you are never rude when I ask for something, so I think we can solve this easily. You also keep the bathroom clean and always pay the rent on time. Let's talk over lunch on Saturday. Thanks for listening!

Best,
Alex

reading.title: Two roommates, two styles
reading.intro: Read the text about two roommates and answer the questions.
paragraphs: When I moved to Guadalajara for my first job, I was nervous about sharing an apartment. My new roommates, Dani and Paco, are very different, and in a few months I learned a lot about them. Now I want to tell you about our strange but happy home.

Dani is incredibly organized. She wakes up early, makes a list every morning and takes her work seriously. She's totally reliable: if she says she'll pay the bill on Friday, she pays it on Friday. She also drives very carefully, so I always feel safe in her car. Her only problem is that she's always telling me to clean the kitchen!

Paco is a completely different person. He's extremely easygoing and a really talented musician. He plays the guitar beautifully, and he has a great sense of humor. But he's pretty disorganized. He's always losing his keys, and he's always borrowing my headphones. He gets impatient in traffic and drives a little recklessly, so I don't ride with him very often. At least he's generous: last week he cooked dinner for the whole building.

At first I thought they were impossible to live with. Now I think the opposite. Dani teaches me to plan my time properly, and Paco shows me how to balance work and play. They aren't perfect, of course. Nobody is. Dani can be a little arrogant when she's right, and Paco is sometimes inconsiderate when he practices at midnight. But they're honest people, and I trust them both.

Last Sunday we had breakfast together for the first time in weeks. Dani talked quickly about her week, Paco listened patiently, and I laughed quietly in the corner of the kitchen. I realized something important: a good home isn't about having the same personality. It's about respecting people who think and act differently, and about saying thank you more often.

listening.title: Who is going to drive?
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two friends. You can replay it.

lines.text: Leo, we need a driver for the trip to Puebla. Should we ask Marco?
Marco? No way. He drives really fast, and he's always honking his horn.
Really? I thought he was careful.
He's a nice guy, but he gets impatient in traffic. What about Sofía?
Sofía drives very carefully, and she's totally reliable.
True. But she's always talking on the phone while she drives.
Seriously? That's not safe at all.
I know. At least she's honest about it, and she always listens when we tell her to stop.
Then let's ask her to drive slowly and keep the phone in her bag.
Good idea. I'll text her now. She's incredibly generous, so she'll probably say yes.
Perfect. I feel much better now.
Me too. This trip is going to be wonderful.
